tagline: Along the South Bay of Grays Harbor to the ocean shore.
intro: SR 105 leaves Aberdeen and heads west along the South Bay of Grays Harbor, passing Ocosta and crossing the Johns River at Markham and then the Elk River. At Cohassett Beach, by Twin Harbors State Park, it turns south down the ocean shore to Grayland, while a four-mile spur goes on north to Westport at the mouth of the harbor. The line drawn here stops south of Grayland, though the state byway, now called Bay-2-Bay, goes on to Raymond.

The road was built in the 1920s to tie Westport and Tokeland to Aberdeen, and the state named the byway for the area's cranberry industry. Westport's marina keeps a large fishing fleet, and cranberries have long been a dependable living here.

moments.title: Westport
moments.text: The Lower Chehalis word for this place was ts-a-lis, the place of sand, and early explorers carried it up the river as Chehalis.

moments.title: Grays Harbor Lighthouse
moments.text: Work on the 107-foot tower began in 1897 about 400 feet from the water's edge, and land built up by the harbor jetties has since left it some 3,000 feet from high tide.

sources.label: State of Washington Tourism, Bay-2-Bay Scenic Byway
